newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currency futures rise as marks correct.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currency futures rise as marks correct.

text.p: IMM currency futures opened mostly higher and extended gains as marks rose on supportive comments from Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer after spot dollar/mark rose to a new four-year high overnight.

Tietmeyer said that it was important the mark enter European Monetary Union as a strong currency and that developments in the foreign exchange markets would be watched. His remarks dragged down dollar/mark after the pair hit a new 41-month high of 1.7665.
Mark futures bounced after setting another in a series of contract lows overnight at $0.5686.
"It's a natural correction that had to happen," said Mike Malpede, senior currency analyst for Refco Group Ltd.
Malpede said marks were also drawing support from a French newspaper report that raised the spectre of France's budget deficit derailing the EMU launch.
Mark and Swiss franc futures added to gains in brisk activity after the 0730 CDT/1230 GMT release of U.S. weekly initial jobless claims, IMM floor traders said.
The Labor Department said claims rose to 377,000 in the week ended July 5, a gain of 40,000 from the previous week, driven by retooling in the automobile industry.
The large increase in claims reinforced sentiment that the Federal Reserve will leave U.S. short-term interest rates steady again at its August policy meeting, an IMM floor trader said.
Yen futures saw choppy action early before turning slightly lower but were holding the overnight low of $0.008928.
British pound futures rose following the Bank of England's decision to raise interest rates 25 basis points to 6.75 percent, the third UK rate increase in three months.

Some floor traders predicted a quiet afternoon ahead for currency futures ahead of Friday's U.S. producer price index data for June. Economists forecast the index unchanged from the previous month, with core PPI excluding food and energy prices rising 0.1 percent.

September yen futures were down $0.000021 at $0.008933, marks up $0.0035 at $0.5744, Swiss francs up $0.0042 at $0.6958, sterling down $0.0034 at $1.6820, Canadian dollars up $0.0009 at $0.7315, Australian dollars down $0.0008 at $0.7455 and Mexican pesos down $0.000125 at $0.123400.
